lead_reading_corrections: audit_passed=False on the qwen winner comes from orchestrator.py:3084 (att.output.audit_passed = att.accepted) ALONE. Not :3148/:3151 -- that branch emits a table_structure_failed audit event with site=post_route_recheck and the page's 8 audit events contain no such event. Not :3180 -- gated on `not ps.is_born_digital`. Not :3580 -- _phase_repair, phase-major only.
ps.native_table_structure_failed=True was set at orchestrator.py:3187 (`if not decision.accepted and self._page_has_tables(...)`), not at :3151.

The judge DID reject, on all five rungs. manifest.json's journal records qwen-local, qwen-cloud, nougat, marker and gemini all with accepted:false. `judge_rejected: false` is a NON-SIGNAL in agentic mode: that field is written in exactly one place, orchestrator.py:3598, inside the phase-major repair judge, which an agentic run never reaches. So the issue's point 1 ('the judge did not reject either') is unsupported.

issue_cited_line_is_wrong.why_not_it: It lives in _run_engine_on_pages, the PHASE-MAJOR path; the repro ran --agentic. And the qwen attempt's status is `success`, so the guard's own predicate is false for it. Same defect SHAPE, did not fire here, left untouched for want of a measured case.

no_native_first_answer.verdict: SAME DEFECT, not a second one
no_native_first_answer.evidence: native_first is read in exactly one decision, orchestrator.py:1491 (_is_trusted_native_without_ocr) -- whether the page is sent to OCR at all. It did that: the page WAS routed and five providers ran on it (manifest.json journal). Nothing downstream of routing reads the flag; _winning_page_output never has. The symptom disappears with this fix.
no_native_first_answer.residue: Documentation only: cli.py:52 help text ('Disable native-first: run VLM on all pages') does not say the flag governs routing only, which is why it reads as broken. No follow-up issue filed.

model output containing NO markdown grid on a table page -> unchanged. This bound is load-bearing: native_table_structure_failed is set at :3187 as a CONSEQUENCE of the ladder failing, not as a measurement of the native text, so it cannot alone justify preferring the model.

left_for_owner: The agentic ladder's rejection reasons are never persisted: manifest.py:662 records `skip_reason or failure_mode.value`, and skip_reason is only set when the output is empty -- hence all five journal rows read reason:'none'. judge_rejected is written only on the phase-major path (orchestrator.py:3598). An agentic run therefore cannot say WHY a rung was refused, which is what sent this issue's own diagnosis to the wrong line. Deserves its own ticket.
orchestrator.py:1451 (the line the issue cited) has the same shape -- `status != SUCCESS` collapses 'errored' with 'flagged' -- but did not fire here and was left alone for want of a measured case.
